objective: Validate model-generated execution plans before durable dispatch with deterministic DAG ordering, critical-path/slack analysis, aggregate budgets, capability coverage, approval barriers, and plan-digest verification.

research.conclusion: Current agent guidance emphasizes multi-step loops, handoffs, guardrails, approvals, tracing, sessions, and resumable workflows.
research.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds a provider-neutral pre-dispatch plan-admission barrier; it does not treat a proposed plan or handoff as execution authority.

research.conclusion: Agent orchestration exposes handoffs, agents-as-tools, guardrails, sessions, MCP integration, tracing, and resumable state.
research.implementation_impact: FAISAL plan admission computes deterministic ordering and approval barriers before existing task, snapshot, and handoff services execute or transfer work.

research.conclusion: MCP defines asynchronous Tasks, capability negotiation, progress/cancellation, and explicit trust and safety boundaries.
research.implementation_impact: MCP-originated tasks and skills remain untrusted plan inputs; admission checks capabilities, budgets, cycles, and approval requirements without executing them.

research.conclusion: Skills are portable instruction sets with progressive discovery and explicit deployment/auth/tool-design decisions.
research.implementation_impact: Skill-derived plans receive the same deterministic DAG and approval analysis and cannot self-authorize irreversible actions.

research.conclusion: The paid-model catalog is changing provider metadata and capability input, not privileged authority.
research.implementation_impact: The plan contract contains no hard-coded provider or model authority and records model metadata outside the authorization boundary.

features: cycle, missing-dependency, duplicate-node, and duplicate-dependency rejection
aggregate CPU and cost budget checking
SHA-256 plan digest and admission verification
separation from task execution, capability granting, and external side effects

benchmark.interpretation: The raw-pass loop is a previous-path proxy that copies/sums plan data without safety analysis. The validated path intentionally costs more because it performs graph checks, deterministic ordering, critical-path/slack analysis, budgets, capability checks, approval-barrier calculation, and SHA-256 digest generation. This is control-plane safety overhead, not an end-to-end inference or agent-throughput claim.

live_model_catalog.interpretation: The catalog was researched for provider-neutral planning and routing design only. No model output, model ID, price, or provider metadata grants authority.

qualification_limits: The subsystem is a bounded userspace/control-plane plan validator; it does not generate plans, call models, execute tasks, grant capabilities, or authorize external side effects.
The benchmark compares plan admission with a raw-pass previous-path proxy and must not be interpreted as a claim of end-to-end latency, throughput, tokens/sec, or cost superiority.
No live paid-model call, MCP server, browser session, robotics device, physical accelerator, production cluster, or operator approval ceremony was used.
The existing task engine remains responsible for task leases, retries, recovery, and persistence; the plan contract is a pre-dispatch analysis layer.
Production approval remains blocked by the established independent builder, signing, physical hardware, secure boot/TPM, live multihost, independent security review, and CVE-ownership requirements.
